extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). Existing datasets were collected with a limit of up to 400 examples per source to ensure balanced representation. New datasets were sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, online education resources, and papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. There may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics, puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, online education resources, and papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation. For the testmini subset, a sampling strategy was adopted: first, randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; then, randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset on its proportion in the entire set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from VQA datasets (examples with numeric answers or quantity words). Expert annotators manually labeled these examples. Quality checks were conducted to address unidentified errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning using majority voting. New datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. A two-step process was used for new datasets: independent annotation by three reviewers, followed by discussion to resolve discrepancies. Expert annotators manually labeled mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples to verify automatic annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in Figure 22, 23, 24)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% for new datasets (only 6 disagreements among 736 questions). Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 for labeling mathematical reasoning. 94.1% exact match between automatic and human annotations for reasoning types.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; Expert annotators
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules for automatic selection; Automatic annotation for mathematical reasoning labels
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination. An online evaluation platform will be maintained. The dataset will be maintained by refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and the leaderboard will be evolved.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Facilitates the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, with applications in educational disciplines, assisting analysts with logical queries, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Focus on specific domains like science and college-level math may limit scalability and generalizability. Annotations lack a unified format and structure due to heterogeneity of sources.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Gaps in representation of certain mathematical problems and visuals. Scalability and generalizability to other domains are a concern. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations. Annotations lack a unified format. The study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models.
